question.problem:
What is ${\int }_{1}^{4}(x+8)^{1/3}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?

*Hint: Write down the missing expression in terms of $i$ and $n.$*

${\int }_{1}^{4}(x+8)^{1/3}\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[($
{{field-1}}
$)^{1/3}\cdot \frac{3}{n}]$
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{1}^{4}(x+8)^{1/3}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=(x+8)^{1/3},$ the lower bound is $a=1$ and the upper bound is $b=4.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{4-1}{n}=\frac{3}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}(x+8)^{1/3}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(1+i\cdot \frac{3}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(1+\frac{3i}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[{((1+\frac{3i}{n})+8)}^{1/3}\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[{(\,9+\frac{3i}{n}\,)}^{1/3}\cdot \frac{3}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
